candidates.title: Prepare answers from a supplied workbook

demandEvidence.chore: Look up requested information in a supplied full spreadsheet workbook.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: There is a zipped full workbook of the spreadsheet as well for the agent to lookup data as needed.

ease.reason: The post supplies a workbook for lookup, but no implementation reference supports workbook question answering.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional analysts may pay for faster workbook lookup; this single post shows no purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A small supplied-workbook mock is bounded, but workbook parsing and answer accuracy are unverified.

autonomy.reason: A person must provide the workbook and verify each answer; no autonomous lookup capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The excerpt identifies a workbook lookup task, but gives no fields, recurrence, constraints, or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Assessed from the exact assigned discussion task and a bounded proposed experiment. The provisional mean is below 6, so this is not proposed for publication.

experimentPlan.output: A cited answer card pointing to workbook sheets or cells relevant to one operator question.
inputs: Synthetic workbook with a few labeled sheets
Expected answer and source cell for checking
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits one question with a supplied workbook.
steps: Load a fictional workbook fixture.
Record one operator question.
Manually select likely supporting cells for the prototype.
Draft a concise answer with sheet and cell references.
Compare it with a prepared expected answer.
Have a person verify every cited cell before use.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For each fixture question, check whether the draft answer matches the expected answer and points to the correct supporting cells.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator supplies the workbook and question; a person validates the answer and references before anyone relies on it.
unverified: Reliable workbook ingestion and cell citation
Handling formulas, hidden sheets, and large workbooks
Whether this lookup task recurs for a paying customer

candidates.title: Organize public signals before installing an app

demandEvidence.chore: Check available information about an app’s security before deciding whether to install it.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’d appreciate any guidance on how to verify an app’s security before installing it in my store.

ease.reason: A source-linked evidence card is approachable, but no implementation source supports automated verification.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: Shopify store operators may value a pre-install review aid; no payment intent is shown.

feasibility.reason: A four-week public-information organizer is bounded, but security criteria and trustworthy verdicts are unsupported.

autonomy.reason: A person must choose sources and make the installation decision; no automated security capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The post asks about security verification before installation, but supplies no method, example app, or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Assessed from the exact assigned discussion task and a bounded proposed experiment. The provisional mean is below 6, so this is not proposed for publication.

experimentPlan.output: A source-linked card separating an app’s public security claims from information the operator could not find.
inputs: Checklist fields selected for the mock
Expected present or missing evidence labels
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator enters public listing text and links for one app under consideration.
steps: Create a fictional app listing fixture.
Enter its public security links.
Extract statements into a source-linked card.
Mark checklist fields as found or not found.
Compare labels with a prepared fixture answer.
Have a person inspect sources and decide whether to install.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Check that each card statement links to its supplied source and that missing fields are labeled unknown rather than unsafe.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator supplies public links; a person judges source quality and makes every security and installation decision.
unverified: Reliable source retrieval or app-security assessment
Whether operators would pay for this aid

candidates.title: Map an agent run’s recovery questions

demandEvidence.chore: Design checkpoint, recovery, and duplicate-safe behavior for an agent run.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: But devs need to write checkpointers, recovery logic, and deal with idempotency by theirselves.

ease.reason: A worksheet can structure a supplied failure case, but no source supports implementing agent recovery behavior.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams building agent workflows may pay for recovery planning; this comment shows no buying intent.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic worksheet fits four weeks, while correct checkpoint and safe retry rules depend on each system.

autonomy.reason: The proposed output is a human-reviewed plan; an engineer must decide and implement every recovery action.

evidence.reason: The comment names checkpointing, recovery logic, and idempotency work, but gives no incident details or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Assessed from the exact assigned discussion task and a bounded proposed experiment. The provisional mean is below 6, so this is not proposed for publication.

experimentPlan.output: A review card listing state to preserve, a proposed restart point, and duplicate-action risks for one fictional failed run.
experimentPlan.trigger: An engineer supplies one fictional interrupted-run case for review.
steps: Create a fictional multi-step agent run.
Mark the state and actions completed before interruption.
Draft questions about restart point and repeated side effects.
Compare questions with a prepared review checklist.
Flag unknown state as unresolved.
Have an engineer choose and test any recovery behavior.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For each fixture, verify that the card identifies known completed actions and marks uncertain state without recommending an unapproved retry.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An engineer supplies the case, checks state assumptions, and authorizes all recovery logic; the prototype never retries or changes an agent.
unverified: Actual checkpoint formats and framework behavior
Safe idempotency rules for a real agent task
Whether this need is recurring or commercially valuable

candidates.title: Compare agent results after a harness change

demandEvidence.chore: Compare financial-agent behavior before and after a harness change.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: We build financial AI agents, and Apgar is the tool we wrote to see whether a harness change made an agent better or worse in production.

ease.reason: A small before-and-after review is possible, but no source documents evaluation implementation or metrics.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: financial-agent teams may pay for regression review; this maker description establishes no buying intent.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic paired-run report is bounded, but meaningful metrics and representative test cases remain unspecified.

autonomy.reason: A script could organize paired results, but a person must define meaningful measures and approve changes.

evidence.reason: The post describes evaluating whether a harness change improved or worsened production agents, with no details or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Assessed from the exact assigned discussion task and a bounded proposed experiment. The provisional mean is below 6, so this is not proposed for publication.

experimentPlan.output: A comparison card showing paired fictional agent outputs and differences against operator-selected checks.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits one paired before-and-after output set for review.
steps: Prepare a fictional financial-agent task fixture.
Enter the two outputs from the same task.
Apply operator-written checks to each output.
List differences and failed checks without inferring causes.
Compare the report with a prepared expected result.
Have an engineer judge significance before changing a harness.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For each fixture pair, check that the report identifies planted differences and does not label a change better or worse without operator-defined criteria.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An engineer supplies representative test cases and decides what counts as a regression; no production agent is called or modified.
unverified: Useful evaluation metrics for a specific financial workflow
Representative test data and safe handling requirements
Any repeat frequency or willingness to pay

candidates.title: Prepare a video edit and publish checklist

demandEvidence.chore: Coordinate recording, editing, and publishing a video.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: You can record, edit and publish with one tool.

ease.reason: The excerpt names a broad video workflow, but no reference supports editing or publishing capabilities.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent video professionals may pay for workflow help; the excerpt establishes no buyer need or purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A checklist mock is feasible, but it does not perform editing or publishing and source details are sparse.

autonomy.reason: A person would record, edit, and publish; no repeatable automated step is supported by the supplied evidence.

evidence.reason: The excerpt only lists product functions and provides no particular chore context, frequency, or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Assessed from the exact assigned discussion task and a bounded proposed experiment. The provisional mean is below 6, so this is not proposed for publication.

experimentPlan.output: A human-reviewed checklist card for one proposed video from recording through a manually completed publish step.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator starts a checklist for one planned video.
steps: Create a fictional video brief.
Enter the current status for recording, editing, and publishing.
Generate a checklist of remaining operator-entered steps.
Compare the checklist with a prepared fixture.
Mark missing status as unknown.
Have a person complete and verify every production action.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Check that the card reflects the supplied status fields and never marks a video published unless the operator entered that status.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person records, edits, uploads, and confirms publication; the mock only organizes operator-entered status.
unverified: Any supported video editing or publishing integration
A repeated customer chore or paying customer hypothesis
